exposure: Groups III and IV (HELLP cases) were compared regarding HELLP classes and outcomes.
outcome: Maternal morbidity (blood transfusion, placental abruption, pulmonary edema, multiple complications)

Fetal and neonatal outcomes (Apgar score, birth weight, NICU admission, intrauterine growth restriction, perinatal death, respiratory distress syndrome, intraventricular hemorrhage, sepsis, need for mechanical ventilation)
cohort: 1238 pregnant women admitted to hypertensive ICU at three university hospitals
finding: Both maternal mortality and morbidity (placental abruption and need for blood transfusion) are significantly higher in women with HELLP syndrome that progresses to class 1 regardless of the presence or absence of eclampsia.
mod_finding: Higher rates of vaginal delivery were reported in women with HELLP (40.9%) and severe PE (39.8%) while higher rates of cesarean section were observed in women with eclampsia (77.8%).
